Safety
sāf´tĭ
n. (security; freedom from danger; Hebrew betach, yesha')
Latin salvus, safe, whole. The Hebrew betach is built on batach, to trust — in Scripture safety and trust are the same root, because safety is a place you are put, not a thing you build.

Biblical Definition

Safety in Scripture is covenantal, and it is nearly always tied to dwelling. The law of jubilee promises it as the fruit of obedience: “Wherefore ye shall do my statutes, and keep my judgments, and do them; and ye shall dwell in the land in safety” (Lev 25:18), and “the land shall yield her fruit, and ye shall eat your fill, and dwell therein in safety” (Lev 25:19). Moses promises it of the settled land: “when he giveth you rest from all your enemies round about, so that ye dwell in safety” (Deu 12:10), and blesses Benjamin with it: “The beloved of the LORD shall dwell in safety by him; and the LORD shall cover him all the day long, and he shall dwell between his shoulders” (Deu 33:12). Proverbs locates it in counsel: “Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety” (Pro 11:14). Job locates it in God's reversal of fortunes: “To set up on high those that be low; that those which mourn may be exalted to safety” (Job 5:11). And David locates it where the word's root does: “I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, LORD, only makest me dwell in safety” (Psa 4:8).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines safety as freedom from danger or hazard; exemption from hurt, injury or loss; preservation from escape.

expand to see more

SAFETY, n. Freedom from danger or hazard; as the safety of an army.

2. Exemption from hurt, injury or loss.

3. Preservation from escape; close custody.

SAFE, a. Free from danger of any kind; as safe from enemies.

Key Scripture

Lev 25:18 — "Wherefore ye shall do my statutes, and keep my judgments, and do them; and ye shall dwell in the land in safety."

Deu 33:12 — "And of Benjamin he said, The beloved of the LORD shall dwell in safety by him; and the LORD shall cover him all the day long, and he shall dwell between his shoulders."

Pro 11:14 — "Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety."

Psa 4:8 — "I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, LORD, only makest me dwell in safety."

Modern Corruption

Safety has become the highest civic and personal value, while Scripture treats it as a gift from God and never as a reason to disobey Him.

expand to see more

The Hebrew settles the matter of where safety comes from: betach, safety, is the noun of batach, to trust. Psalm 4:8 makes the identity explicit — thou, LORD, only makest me dwell in safety — and David wrote it while men were saying, Who will shew us any good. Safety in Scripture is not the absence of enemies. It is the presence of a Keeper, and a man can lie down and sleep in it while the danger is still outside.

That ordering is what the present age has inverted. Safety has become the value to which others are subordinated, so that risk itself is treated as a wrong to be eliminated rather than a cost to be weighed. Scripture's men are told to dwell in safety and are also sent into danger; Paul stood in jeopardy every hour, and the Hebrew midwives feared God rather than the king. A safety that requires disobedience is not the thing Leviticus promised. Proverbs 11:14 gives the practical means, and it is corporate: in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew betach (H983), safety, security; from batach (H982), to trust; yesha' (H3468), salvation or safety, in Job 5:11 and Proverbs 21:31.

expand to see more

Hebrew betach (H983) — safety, securely; Leviticus 25:18, Deuteronomy 33:12, Psalm 4:8.

Hebrew batach (H982) — to trust, to be confident; the root of the noun.

Hebrew yesha' (H3468) — safety, salvation; Job 5:11, exalted to safety.

Hebrew teshu'ah (H8668) — deliverance, safety; Proverbs 11:14, in the multitude of counsellors.

Hebrew shakan (H7931) — to dwell; safety in Scripture is nearly always a dwelling.

Usage

"“Thou, LORD, only makest me dwell in safety” — and he lay down and slept."

"“In the multitude of counsellors there is safety” — a corporate means."

"“The beloved of the LORD shall dwell in safety by him” — by Him, not by walls."
